_comment: Curated A15 test-point data, hand-authored from the 1996 service manual rather
than parsed. Like A14, this board generates no supply that Chapter 2 tabulates:
there is no Table 2-x for it. The only rails it makes for itself are the +/-20 S
pair that VR3 and VR4 shunt-regulate out of +/-44 S, and the only published
expectation for those is §5-21 step 2 -- at the zener leads, not at a test point.
So almost every number here comes from the fourteen steps of §5-21, and the ones
that are not at a test point are the probePoints below.
Signal names and the sheet/zone references beside them are transcribed from the
legend box at the bottom right of schematic sheet 1, which prints them as
'TP1 = INPUT (PG1D7)' -- page 1, zone D7. All eleven derived zones agree with
the printed ones, which is an independent check on the placements.
TP7 (ACOM) is the reference for every measurement on this board unless a step
says otherwise -- §5-21 step 1. TP9 and TP10 are the exception: the VI rails
return to VI COM at P602 pins 17A/17C, which is not a test point on this board,
so they carry no refPoint and say so in their condition instead.
Two entries are marked inferred and it is worth knowing why. TP9 and TP10 carry
the +/-5.3 V +/-10% that §5-19 step 9 publishes for the same two nets one board
away, at A14's P612 pins 15A/C and 14A/C. A15 has no published figure of its own
for them; the net is the same wire through the motherboard, and the condition is
reproduced exactly, but the reading was specified at A14's connector and that is
recorded rather than hidden.
TP5's ac check is deliberately not written as a band. §5-21 step 8 asks for a
ratio -- measure HR7 resistor network pin 1, then verify TP5 is 1/100th of the
voltage you just noted -- so the published expectation lives on the HR7 pin 1
probe point, and TP5 keeps only the one number the manual states outright.
Step numbers are §5-21's own; the section prints all fourteen as one sequence.

HV.label: DC HV amplifier and series pass

testpoints.note: The input to the dc HV amplifier, at the far end of the 1 kohm resistor R1 from the node that K1 and the 70 kohm end of the HR7 network share. R1 carries no current into a meter, so the drop across it is negligible. In the 1100 V dc range DAC OUT HI and DAC SENSE HI are tied together and connected to that node by relay K1, and the assembly amplifies it by -100 -- so -2.2 V here is the 220 V output the instrument was asked for. The band is tight (+/-1 mV on 2.2 V) because it is really a check on K1 and on the DAC, not on this board's gain. Nothing here at all points at K1 and its drive circuit, which live on A14.

The only high-voltage test point on the board, and the only one that is a socket rather than a wire loop -- a single PWB socket for an 0.080 pin. It sits on the 7 Mohm end of the HR7 network through the 100 kohm resistor R2, which is the same node §5-21 step 8 calls 'pin 1 of the HR7 resistor network'. That series resistor is the reason no number is recorded here: with a 10 Mohm meter it costs about 1% of the reading, which is twenty times the +/-0.1 V band step 8 asks for. Use TP2 to see whether high voltage is present; use HR7 pin 1 to measure it.

HVAMP OUT, the output of U2 -- the fast LF356 that follows the HR7 hybrid's own op amp and adds gain and slew rate. This is the node the diagnostics watch as well: it is divided by R18 and R19 into HV MUX2, which is what fault codes 3109 and 3113 read. §5-21 steps 4 and 5 use TP3 for polarity only, against TP5 and against HR7 pin 10.

One of the two series-pass control nodes. -SP C is made on A14 from the opposite HVDC rail by its relays K4 and K8 and clamped to 16 V by VR1 here, but its dc level is set by this board's series-pass circuit: Q3's collector pulls it toward PACOM, which makes A14's magnitude control raise HVCL. §2-159 says +/-SP C sit at approximately +/-6.8 V in normal operation, which is the -220 V dc case below; the standby and +220 V readings are higher because Q3 is not conducting.

states.label: Power-up, 0 V standby
states.setup: Set the Calibrator to 0 V standby.

testpoints.note: Recorded in microvolts rather than volts, because that is the range you would actually use and because 0.00005 V rounds to nothing in a display. The manual's words are '0V ±50 µV'. The output of U1, the op amp that inverts HVAMP OUT so the signal reaching OSC SENSE HI is in phase with the Oscillator output. U1 is switched into circuit by K9, K8B and K6 and is only used in the ac function. Two more checks use TP5 without giving it a level of its own: step 4 verifies it is the opposite polarity to TP3, and step 8, in the 1100 V ac range at 220 V and 130 Hz, verifies it reads 1/100th of whatever was measured at HR7 resistor network pin 1. That second one is a ratio, not a band, so the number lives on the HR7 pin 1 probe point instead. Failing step 3 sends you to step 4; passing it skips to step 6.

The mirror of TP4. +SP C is controlled by Q6 when the high-voltage output is positive, clamped by VR2 through R24, and is the node whose dc level tells A14's magnitude loop how hard to drive the HVDC supplies. The two polarities are not symmetric in the readings because only one of Q3 and Q6 is doing the work at a time.

states.label: Power-up, 0 V standby
states.setup: Set the Calibrator to 0 V standby.

testpoints.note: Analog common, and the reference for every measurement on this assembly unless a step says otherwise. ACOM is not permanently tied to anything: relay K3 connects it to RCOM in the dc voltage function, and K3 with K4A connect it to OSC RCOM in the ac function, so the board's own common is switched with the range.

Power amplifier common, the return for the series-pass circuit and for the high-voltage supplies arriving from A14. CR5 and CR6, a back-to-back pair of 1N4002s, sit between ACOM and PACOM to keep the two commons within a diode drop of each other. §5-21 references its measurements to ACOM (TP7), not to this point.

testpoints.condition: 220 mA at 1 kHz, operate, with the front panel OUTPUT HI binding post jumpered to OUTPUT LO. DMM low lead on VI COM at P602 pins 17A/17C -- not on ACOM.
testpoints.source: §5-19 step 9 (A14), for the same net at P612 pins 15A/C; Figure 7-18 sheet 1 legend (PG2B6)
testpoints.note: The positive half of the low-voltage, high-current supply pair that feeds the 2.2 A output stage. It is made on A14 -- stepped-down T1 secondary, rectified by CR5 there and filtered by C3 -- and arrives here at P602 18A/18C, filtered again by C37 and C38. §5-21 publishes no figure for it, so the +/-10% band is A14's, measured at A14's connector on the same wire; it is marked inferred for that reason. Its magnitude is deliberately held down by the magnitude control loop to keep the collector-emitter voltage low on Q11 and Q14, so it is not a fixed rail and the reading only means anything at the stated output. Remove the front-panel jumper afterwards.

testpoints.condition: 220 mA at 1 kHz, operate, with the front panel OUTPUT HI binding post jumpered to OUTPUT LO. DMM low lead on VI COM at P602 pins 17A/17C -- not on ACOM.
testpoints.source: §5-19 step 9 (A14), for the same net at P612 pins 14A/C; Figure 7-18 sheet 1 legend (PG2A6)
testpoints.note: The negative half of the pair, arriving at P602 19A/19C and filtered by C39 and C40. VI+ sources the output current and VI- sinks it. Same inference and the same caution as TP9: the published band was specified at A14's connector, and the level tracks the output rather than standing still.

The output of the H4 hybrid: a voltage directly proportional to the output current of the 2.2 A range. Nothing on this board publishes a level for it, and it is not a level you would score -- it is the reference for two checks elsewhere. §5-20 step 4 on A14 tells you to note the amplitude of its positive peaks and then verify A14's absolute value output equals them, and fault codes 3119, 3120, 3139 and 3140 all measure the result of feeding G OUT into A14's absolute value circuit. Q22 with R72-R76 forms a high-frequency path around it for loop stability.

probePoints.label: VR3 cathode (+20 S)
probePoints.note: The board's own positive local supply. +44 S arrives at P602 28A/28C, drops through the 2 kohm half-watt R31, and VR3 shunt-regulates the result to 20 V with C15 across it. It is the supply for U1, the ac sense buffer inverter, so a fault here presents as a dead buffer rather than as a supply fault.

probePoints.label: VR4 anode (-20 S)
probePoints.note: The negative half, from -44 S at P602 29A/29C through R32 and clamped by VR4, with C16 across it. The manual prints the expectation as '-20V +/-5%', already signed, which is not something Chapter 2's supply tables do -- there the magnitudes are printed unsigned.

probePoints.label: HR7 resistor network pin 1 (7 Mohm end)
probePoints.condition: 220 V at 130 Hz, operate. 1100 V ac range.
probePoints.note: The high-voltage side of the HR7 network in the ac function, where INT HV SNS arrives through K6. Note the reading, then check that TP5 is 1/100th of it -- that ratio is what the 7 Mohm input and 70 kohm feedback resistors set, and it is what the whole ac range's accuracy rests on. 130 Hz is chosen because it is above the 120 Hz point where A14's K14-K16 series the transformer windings. If the instrument keeps tripping to standby, jumper TP9 to TP10 on the DAC assembly (A11) first, and remove that jumper before step 9.

probePoints.label: HR7 hybrid pin 10
probePoints.note: Checked for polarity, not level: note the polarity here, then verify TP3 is the opposite. Pin 10 is one of the two 300 ohm inputs to the LT1052 chopper-stabilised amplifier inside the HR7 hybrid, so this is the step that separates a dead hybrid from a dead U2.

probePoints.label: H4 hybrid output (R42 / R44 / H4 pin 18)
probePoints.condition: Hybrid cover removed, right-hand end of R37 unsoldered and lifted, an external ac reference of 1 V at 1 kHz injected there, assembly on the extender card.
probePoints.note: Scope point. The manual gives a waveform, not a level: expect a square wave like Figure 5-32, which it draws at 1 V and 10 ms per division. Nothing is scored here because nothing is published to score. The lifted end of R37 is the node with Z5 pins 2 and 3, labelled G+ on the schematic. Resolder R37 and refit the H4 cover before continuing -- leaving the cover off changes the oven's thermal environment and will upset fault codes 3104 and 3105.

probePoints.label: U3B pin 7
probePoints.condition: As the H4 output check: R37 lifted and driven from an external 1 V, 1 kHz reference.
probePoints.conflict: §5-21 step 13 says this pin shows a square wave equal to the *positive* peaks of Figure 5-32; §2-161's circuit description makes U3B's output the half wave equal to the *negative* peaks. Both are recorded -- see the caveat.
probePoints.note: Scope point, described as a waveform and never as a level. §2-161 has U3B subtracting U3A's half wave from the H4 signal to leave the half wave equal to the negative peaks, with R45 holding it about 0.7 V below 0 V; Q15 and R50 turn that into the current U4 amplifies through the Darlington pair Q11/Q12. §5-21 step 13 calls the same trace the positive peaks. Whichever way round the sign is described, what the step is testing is that a half wave appears here at all.

probePoints.label: U3A pin 1
probePoints.condition: As the H4 output check: R37 lifted and driven from an external 1 V, 1 kHz reference.
probePoints.conflict: §5-21 step 13 says this pin shows the *negative* peaks of Figure 5-32; §2-161 makes U3A the stage that produces the half wave equal to the *positive* peaks. See the caveat.
probePoints.note: Scope point, described as a waveform. §2-161: U3A creates the half wave equal to the positive peaks of the H4 signal, with R47 holding it about 0.7 V above 0 V, and Q16 with R48 turn it into the current U5 amplifies through Q13/Q14. In the dc current function only one of the two halves is ever active -- outputting positive current makes the H4 voltage negative, so U3A's output sits at zero -- which is why a dc-only fault can leave one of these two traces looking dead and be perfectly correct.

probePoints.label: Across R57 (0.1 ohm sense, U5 side)
probePoints.condition: 0 A called up with the instrument range-locked in the 2.2 A range. Measured across the resistor, not to ACOM.
probePoints.note: The quiescent current in the Q13/Q14 half of the output stage: 0.028 V across 0.1 ohm is about 280 mA, standing in the pair even with no output called for. R57 is paralleled by R77, and the voltage across them is forced to follow the voltage across the 191 ohm R56 -- a 1000:1 ratio. A reading far off here with R68 correct points at U5 or its Darlington rather than at anything common.

probePoints.label: Across R68 (0.1 ohm sense, U4 side)
probePoints.condition: 0 A called up with the instrument range-locked in the 2.2 A range. Measured across the resistor, not to ACOM.
probePoints.note: The same check for the other half: R68 is paralleled by R78 and tracks the 191 ohm R69 in the same 1000:1 ratio, driven by U4 through the Darlington pair Q11/Q12. Both halves out of band together is a supply or a bias problem; one of the two is a channel problem.
